The presence of two different mediators—Glycine and Clofedanol—underscores the complexity of the relationship, suggesting that Dihydrocodeine may interact with multiple pathways that contribute to pharyngitis. The integration of these pathways supports the hypothesis that Dihydrocodeine could be a potential repurposed drug for pharyngitis, though further research is needed to clarify the exact mechanism and clinical relevance.
